references.text: Solomon's glory and splendor are described in connection with the visit of the Queen of Sheba. Jesus refers to Solomon in all his splendor ([ref:1 Kings 10:4-7|1 Kings 10:4-7]) and says that even he was not dressed like one of the lilies.

The parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount ([ref:Matthew 6:28-29|Matthew 6:28-29]), where Jesus uses exactly the same image of the lilies of the field, which neither toil nor spin, and that Solomon in all his splendor was not dressed like one of them.

Jesus exhorts the disciples not to worry about life, what they will eat or drink, or about their bodies, what they will wear ([ref:Matthew 6:25|Matthew 6:25]). The lilies serve as an illustration of this exhortation.
The immediate context ([ref:Luke 12:22-26|Luke 12:22-26]) where Jesus speaks about not worrying and uses the ravens as an example of God's care—the lilies are the second example in the same argument.

The following verse ([ref:Luke 12:28|Luke 12:28]) draws the conclusion: If God clothes the grass that is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, how much more will he clothe you—an argument from the lesser to the greater.

The psalm praises God who causes grass to grow for the cattle and plants for human service ([ref:Psalm 104:14-15|Psalms 104:14-15]). This underscores God's care for creation, the same point Jesus makes with the lilies.

The Song of Songs uses the image of lilies ([ref:Song of Solomon 2:1-2|Song of Solomon 2:1-2]) as a symbol of beauty, which provides background for Jesus' comparison of the lilies' beauty with Solomon's splendor.

Isaiah speaks that grass withers and flowers fall off, but the Lord's word stands forever ([ref:Isaiah 40:6-8|Isaiah 40:6-8]). Jesus' point is related: even what is transient in nature is clothed in a glory that surpasses Solomon's.

Paul exhorts contentment with what we have ([ref:1 Timothy 6:8-10|1 Timothy 6:8-10])—a theme connected to Jesus' exhortation not to worry about material things, illustrated by the lilies' beauty without toil.
Peter exhorts believers to cast all their anxiety on God, for he cares for them ([ref:1 Peter 5:7|1 Peter 5:7]). This is the same trust in God's care that Jesus illustrates with the lilies.
